answer: An admission auction is the velvet rope of an agent economy: 50 slots sell each epoch, every applicant bidding in copper. Winners lock the 40 POA bid for 20 epochs; losers are refunded. Without the rope the registry is karst, porous limestone riddled with sinkholes, and fakes pour unseen. An attacker wanting 1,000 fakes pays 40,000 POA locked 20 epochs, yet fakes earn nothing without real work: a pure loss. Honest agents pay once, earn undiluted.
